key_insight: MamaBench shows that medical LLMs can answer the original case correctly yet still fail clinically similar counterfactual cases, revealing a gap between benchmark accuracy and true diagnostic robustness.
clinical_relevance: For maternal and child health AI, this matters because small changes in presentation can imply different interventions, so systems need to distinguish near-miss cases reliably.
method: Created MamaBench: 434 expert-authored clinical narratives in 217 counterfactual pairs across 371 pathologies.
Evaluated models with Bias Trap Rate (BTR), measuring the chance of failing the counterfactual after succeeding on the base case.
Introduced Evidence-Anchored RAG (EA-RAG), which extracts clinical parameters, audits evidence coverage, and uses contrastive sub-queries.
evidence_signal: Across eight configurations of four frontier LLMs, base accuracy overstated robust accuracy by 16–28 percentage points; EA-RAG achieved 20.3% BTR and 65.0% robust accuracy on Claude Sonnet 4.6.
watch_item: Even with EA-RAG, a residual 20% BTR remains, so counterfactual robustness is still incomplete and should not be assumed from standard benchmark scores.
paper_title: MamaBench: Benchmarking LLM Robustness in Maternal and Child Health Diagnosis through Counterfactual Clinical Perturbation
